title: When the Autopsy Wakes
premise: August Nakamura, a retired detective who buried their past under the quiet routine of a failing bookshop, is pulled back when a corpse is found wearing clothes stolen from the closet of the case's sole surviving witness—August's estranged former partner, Iris Vale. The body belongs to a man officially declared dead ten years ago in the case August was forced to close, meaning someone faked a death and someone else has been keeping him hidden. As August and Iris reopen old files and older wounds, they discover the town's most respected family orchestrated both deaths to protect a secret that would destroy them. In the end, August must choose between exposing the truth and protecting Iris, who turns out to have been complicit all along; they choose the truth, and love survives it—barely—when Iris surrenders herself as August watches.
about_author: Jonah Kavanagh is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent seven years covering crime beats before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who thought they had escaped their pasts.

chapters.title: Alphabetical Silence
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from August's POV. We meet August shelving books in a shop drowning in debt, a person who has made invisibility an art. A knock at the door: Detective Reyes, asking August to identify a body. The emotional beat is dread disguised as calm—the past knocking on glass.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: At the morgue, August recognizes the victim: Daniel Okafor, declared dead a decade ago in the case August closed under pressure. Stranger still, he wears clothes stolen from Iris Vale's closet. POV shifts to Reyes. The beat: vertigo—a closed case cracking open like a rib cage.

chapters.title: What Iris Kept
chapters.summary: August visits Iris, now a hospice nurse living carefully, and their reunion is all deflection and unfinished sentences. She claims she never met Okafor, but her hands shake. August's POV. The beat: longing sharpened by suspicion—love against duty begins its argument.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, August's POV, reconstructing the original case: Okafor's 'death,' the town's relief, the pressure from above to close it. Present-day August realizes the file was curated, not completed. The beat: grief for the detective they used to be, and anger at who made them stop.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Trap
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the shop but takes nothing—only rearranges books alphabetically by title, a message meant for August alone. Reyes grows wary of August's involvement; the town council hints the shop's lease could vanish. August's POV. Beat: paranoia blooming in a familiar room.

chapters.title: A Second Body
chapters.summary: The coroner who signed Okafor's original death certificate is found drowned, staged as an accident. Reyes's POV reveals she's been ordered off the case by the mayor's office. She quietly shares her file with August anyway. Beat: two lonely investigators choosing each other over institutions.

chapters.title: The Holloway Ledger
chapters.summary: Following money trails, August finds payments routed through the Holloway family's foundation—to Iris, monthly, for ten years. Confrontation: Iris admits she witnessed something the night Okafor 'died' and was paid for silence. August's POV. Beat: betrayal arriving dressed as protection.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: August pieces it together: Senator Marcus Holloway killed Okafor a decade ago, faked the death, and has now killed again because Okafor came back to blackmail him. The stolen clothes were planted to frame Iris. August's POV, racing. Beat: clarity arriving too fast, danger closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Closing Time
chapters.summary: Climax. Holloway's fixer comes for Iris at the hospice; August arrives mid-abduction and a brutal confrontation ends with the fixer arrested and Holloway exposed via a recorded confession Iris baited herself—her own act of courage. August's POV. Beat: duty and love finally pulling the same direction.

chapters.title: Shelved, Not Buried
chapters.summary: Resolution. Holloway indicted; Iris, charged with obstruction, accepts a plea and a sentence she refuses to let August fight. In the epilogue-tinged final scene, August reopens the shop with a new section: true crime, honestly told. Beat: bittersweet peace—identity rebuilt not by forgetting, but by telling the truth.
